comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 (SBE Bachelor Education and Examination Regulations 2026-2027, Article 16.9, for students starting in September 2026; programme pages checked 2026-10-02)
comparator.sourceNotes: The programme pages (s1 Courses & curriculum, s2, s3, s4) name the courses of the three-year English-taught BSc in Maastricht but are labelled 2024-2025 and give no EC; the course catalogue could not be read from this environment. The 180-EC reconstruction therefore follows the SBE Bachelor Education and Examination Regulations 2026-2027 (s0), which publish the 2026-2027 outline for International Business: Article 16.3 sets the first year at eight compulsory 6.5-EC courses and two 4.0-EC skills trainings (60 EC); Article 16.9 sets semesters 3 and 4 at eight compulsory 6.5-EC courses, one compulsory 4.0-EC skills training (Quantitative Methods III) and one elective 4.0-EC skills training (60 EC); and semesters 5 and 6 at a 26-EC study abroad period, two major courses and one elective course of 6.5 EC each, two 2.0-EC Professional Development skills trainings (Global Citizenship Skills and Leadership Skills), the 2.5-EC thesis skills training and the 8.0-EC Bachelor's thesis (60 EC). The programme page lists Reflections on Academic Discourse in year 1 (2024-2025); the regulations list Philosophy of Science (EBS1001) for 2026-2027 and were followed. The regulations note that the outline may change in 2027-2028. Majors: students choose one of eight majors of two courses each (Accounting, Finance, Information Management, Supply Chain Management, Marketing, Organisation, Strategy, Entrepreneurship); the major courses and elective lists are published only on the SBE Student Intranet, so the major, the elective and the elective skills training are kept as explicit restricted-choice components without named courses. The Accounting variants and the Entrepreneurship exception change only the distribution of the same 60 EC. Course content below the title level is not published on readable pages, so comparison matches were made on the subject named by each component. Checked 2026-10-02. A human may wish to confirm the matches against the course catalogue.

alternatives.concept: The strongest defensible UCR response to the Bachelor International Business at Maastricht University (regular programme, no specialisation), which combines management of organisations, marketing and strategy, accounting and finance, global business and corporate governance, supply chains, operations and product development, management information systems, entrepreneurship, quantitative methods, a study abroad semester, a major in one business discipline and a thesis. UCR offers business courses in marketing, strategy, accounting and corporate finance, finance, international business and governance, transnational business law, leadership, negotiation, entrepreneurship, product design and AI and business, with economics, econometrics, data science, ethics and communication as specific complementary contributions; it offers no supply-chain, operations-management, management-information-systems or corporate-governance course, and those components are not replaced by the courses used here.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum has four business-function courses in marketing, strategy and the management of organisations (Marketing & Consumer Engagement, Strategy & Digital Transformation, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Market Research), two accounting and finance courses, four economics and international-business courses (Introduction to Economics, International Macroeconomics, International Business & Governance, Transnational Business Law), four leadership, negotiation and communication courses, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations and Consumer Product Design, three research-methods, econometrics and data courses plus Database Management Systems, and further courses on AI and business, ethics and circular economy together with Personal & Professional Development. The label names the business, economics, leadership and entrepreneurship core with the business-law and data strands without presenting any one strand as the whole programme.

alternatives.concept: The Emerging Markets specialisation of the Bachelor International Business studies economic development and business opportunities in emerging economies together with their socio-economic, historical, cultural and political context, and prepares for responsible management and policy decisions in those economies. UCR has no emerging-markets, development-economics or regional-business course, so this alternative implements the evidenced multidisciplinary idea rather than the specialisation: economics and international business supply the economic and business core, and political, sociological, historical, legal and sustainability courses with global and Global South perspectives supply the context. The adjacent courses are specific complementary contributions and not substitutes for the specialisation's emerging-economies content.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum has seven business and economics courses (Introduction to Economics, International Macroeconomics, Public Economics, Econometrics, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, International Business & Governance, Transnational Business Law), three politics and international-relations courses, five sociology and history courses on colonial and Global South contexts, two law courses (Law, Society & Justice and Public International Law), three sustainability courses on governance, food supply chains and circular economy, Ethics, Leadership & Diversity Management, Research Methods & Statistics and Personal & Professional Development. The label therefore names the business and economics core together with the political, social, legal and sustainability context instead of presenting emerging markets or business alone as the whole programme, and the label's emerging-economies framing refers to the perspective of the courses, not to a dedicated development-economics curriculum.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Alternative 1 organises the programme around the functions of an international firm (marketing, strategy, accounting and finance, leadership, operations and product development, information and entrepreneurship). Alternative 2 changes the organising question to how politics, culture, history and law shape business and economic development in emerging economies, which is the evidenced direction of the target's formal Emerging Markets specialisation. That change has material curricular consequences: marketing, strategy, accounting, finance, negotiation, product design, market research, database and data-science courses are replaced by comparative politics, international relations, peace and conflict, three sociology courses, history of empires, public international law, Public Economics and two sustainability courses on food supply chains and governance. The programmes share 11 courses and differ by 13 courses each, so every pair passes the 30 EC / 4-course floor in both directions.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Bachelor International Business. The 2026-2027 SBE Education and Examination Regulations (Article 16.9) offer two formal routes, the regular programme with no specialisation and the Emerging Markets specialisation (IB-EM), which requires a separate enrolment procedure, an internship in an emerging economy and a different third-year structure. The regular programme is the general route that every International Business student follows unless they enrol in the specialisation, so it best represents the programme's broad academic identity and is also the least specialized route; the choice was made before UCR fit was considered. Within the regular route, the eight third-year majors have equal formal standing and their individual courses are published only on the SBE Student Intranet, so the major is left as an explicit restricted choice instead of being instantiated.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Every formal prerequisite is scheduled in an earlier semester: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations in semester 1 precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation, Transnational Business Law, International Business & Governance, Market Research and Money, Banking & Finance; Research Methods & Statistics in semester 2 precedes International Macroeconomics, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, Marketing & Consumer Engagement, Econometrics and Leadership & Diversity Management. Introduction to Economics, Personal Leadership and the entrepreneurship and methods foundations come first, the strategy and accounting courses follow in semesters 2 and 3, and the econometrics, finance, market-research and diversity-management courses close the programme in semester 6. Accounting & Corporate Finance is placed in semester 3 because the semester 1 and 2 slots are fixed by availability.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two UCR alternatives are defensible and production stopped at two. Alternative 1 owns thirteen generator-eligible rows that describe the target's own core (6035 to 6045 on international business and global markets, how international companies are managed, strategy, marketing, accounting and financial decision-making, supply chains and sourcing, managing employees, business law and taxation, business ethics, globalisation and business information management; 6047 on leadership in international organisations; 6048 on cross-cultural business communication). Alternative 2 is built on the five stable study directions in emerging markets (6050 to 6054), which are the target's formal Emerging Markets specialisation and form one coherent direction on economic development and the political and cultural context of business; it shares 11 courses with Alternative 1 and differs by 13 courses each way, so it passes the 30 EC / 4-course floor. A third concept was assessed on the formal Organisation major (people, leadership, negotiation and cross-cultural communication), supported by rows 6041, 6047, 6048 and 6049. Its evidence is already substantively covered by Alternative 1, which contains Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Personal Leadership, Leadership & Diversity Management, Negotiation & Strategic Thinking and Persuasive Communication; a separate programme would keep those courses and replace the business-function courses with general psychology, rhetoric and behavioural-economics courses that the evidence does not tie to the target, so it was rejected as not-substantively-distinct. The Supply Chain Management major (row 6040) was rejected as not-feasible: UCR has no supply-chain, logistics or operations-management course (only Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy and Consumer Product Design touch the area, both already in Alternative 1), so the differing courses would be an assortment. The remaining majors (Accounting, Finance, Information Management, Marketing, Strategy and Entrepreneurship) are covered by the business-function courses of Alternative 1 and describe no different organising logic.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both address how organisations function and are managed; Psychology of Organizations & Leadership approaches this through organisational behaviour, motivation, group dynamics, culture and leadership, rather than through management theory or organisational design.

Both address marketing management; Marketing & Consumer Engagement covers consumer behaviour, marketing strategy, digital marketing and brand strategy with marketing plans, without a cross-country focus.
Both address business strategy; Strategy & Digital Transformation has students develop a strategic plan from vision to execution, with a digital-technology emphasis.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Management of Organisations and Marketing introduces organisations and marketing together; the UCR courses on each half are aligned with the larger Management of Organisations and Marketing Management components, and no further UCR course is a sufficiently direct counterpart.

Both develop leadership skills; Personal Leadership introduces transformational and authentic leadership with self-awareness and practical skills, which is the specific function of the Professional Development: Leadership Skills training, although it is a full course rather than a short training.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Management Game is a team-based management simulation skills training, and no scheduled UCR course is a sufficiently direct counterpart; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations is a venture-creation course aligned with Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management.
Both teach financial reporting; Accounting & Corporate Finance covers accounting theory and practice with emphasis on using and analysing financial statements and annual reports.

Both address financial decision-making; Money, Banking & Finance teaches analysing financial data, assessing risk and taking investment and budgeting decisions, without the full corporate-finance sequence of a finance course.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Managerial Finance and Accounting is a second-year course on management accounting and corporate finance; UCR's accounting and finance courses are already aligned with Accounting and Financial Reporting and Finance, and no other UCR course addresses managerial accounting.

Both give the economic foundations for business; Introduction to Economics covers micro- and macroeconomics, which is the economics part of Economics and Business, without the business-context applications.

Both address international business; International Business & Governance examines the institutional, political and cultural forces shaping global businesses, global trade and cross-border governance, which is the central subject of Global Business.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Corporate Governance is a dedicated second-year course on the governance of firms; International Business & Governance covers cross-border governance but is already aligned with Global Business, and no other scheduled UCR course addresses corporate governance.

Both address product development; Consumer Product Design has teams take a consumer product from customer needs to prototype, which matches the product-development half of the component but has no operations-management content.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Fundamentals of Supply Chain Management has no UCR counterpart; Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy addresses the life cycle of products from raw materials to reuse but not logistics, sourcing or supply-chain management.

Both address the management of business data; Database Management Systems covers relational databases, SQL and normalisation, which is the data-management part of Management Information Systems, without information-systems strategy or business-process content.

Both address starting and running a small venture; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations has teams develop a venture from idea to final pitch with market validation and business planning, without the small-business management content of the component.

notes.text: Both programmes include substantial study of international business, management, marketing and finance. The Bachelor International Business additionally includes specialist work in supply chain management, operations and product development, management information systems, corporate governance and a major in a chosen business discipline, with a study abroad semester. UCR students can instead combine business, economics, leadership and entrepreneurship courses with courses from other disciplines, but those specialist components are not offered at the same level of depth.

The Bachelor International Business combines accounting, finance, marketing, strategy, supply chain management and information management with a study abroad semester. At UCR, students can approach international business and emerging economies through fields such as economics, politics, sociology, law and sustainability. These programmes therefore offer related perspectives rather than reproducing a full international business curriculum.
